strengths: The per-orientation accuracy maps reveal structure that average OoD accuracy conceals: generalization concentrates around familiar views, in-plane rotations, and certain silhouette-preserving transformations. These findings have an identifiable audience in visual robustness and representation learning.

The empirical investigation includes substantial controls: three object categories, cross-category transfer, several architectures, alternative training orientations, pretraining, and augmentation. Keeping the training-image budget constant and repeating experiments with five sampled instance splits strengthen the descriptive findings.

The geometric model provides an interpretable account of the observed accuracy patterns, supported by component ablations and high reported correlations. The experimental paradigm and visualizations are understandable, and the manuscript identifies a code/data repository.
weaknesses: Necessary—align mechanistic claims with the evidence. The abstract states that dissemination is achieved through neurons tuned to common features, and the Discussion concludes that biological recognition mechanisms largely apply to DNNs. Figures 4 and S.7 establish activation similarities and correlations, but do not identify the proposed transfer mechanism or distinguish it from shared sensitivity to image geometry under joint training. Targeted interventions with suitable controls could strengthen this interpretation; alternatively, consistently present dissemination as a hypothesis supported by observational evidence and qualify the biological conclusions.

Necessary—validate the invariance measurement. Equations 5–7 compare activations averaged across orientation sets, so equal means can produce maximal invariance despite substantial variation between individual views. Moreover, requiring both means to exceed the activity threshold excludes neurons that respond strongly to familiar views but become silent in novel views—precisely a failure of invariance. The resulting conditional score does not establish invariance of the overall representation. Report retained fractions and verify the conclusions with view-level measurements that include response-loss cases and assess threshold sensitivity.

Necessary—distinguish fitted descriptions from independently validated predictions. Section 4.2 optimizes Pearson correlation against measured accuracy, but describes no separate fitting and evaluation split. Consequently, the reported correlations above 0.8 demonstrate goodness of fit, without establishing predictive performance on independent observations. The generalizable/non-generalizable partition is also derived from this fitted model, so its accuracy separation is not independent validation. Evaluate on withheld runs, instances, or orientation regions, or narrow the claims to descriptive fitting and establish the partition’s robustness.

Necessary—complete the evaluation reporting. The manuscript provides training sizes and hyperparameters but leaves the test-rendering protocol, samples per orientation bin, and meaning of plotted error bars insufficiently specified. Learning rates are selected partly using OoD behavior, without identifying a separate validation set. Clarify these details and distinguish validation from final evaluation; the current description does not establish that leakage occurred, but does leave the assessment difficult to audit.

Optional—extend and improve presentation. Experiments with varied lighting, backgrounds, or real images would help establish the scope beyond centered synthetic objects, but are not required for a suitably bounded empirical contribution. Larger plot labels and fuller supplementary captions would also improve usability.
